To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed, built and experimentally characterized a self-adjusting knee joint exoskeleton that is able to accommodate the natural movements of the human knee joint and to provide active assistance to the patient during the rehabilitation exercises, thus enabling a robot-assisted rehabilitation of knee joint injuries.
we developed a new device for robot-assist rehabilitation of knee injuries that can automatically adjust its joint axes and is capable of providing high torques to the knee joint.
a novel active device has been designed, built and tested, featuring automatic adjustability of joint axes and a compact design.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new device to be used for rehabilitation of knee injuries.

the design and development of a novel active knee exoskeleton that is capable of supporting both translational and rotational movements of the human knee joint, thus enabling more effective robot-assisted rehabilitation.
the design and implementation of a new robotic device for knee rehabilitation that is able to automatically adjust its axes of rotation, allowing a perfect match with the patient's joint axes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed device is an effective tool to be utilized for robot-assisted gait rehabilitation of patients with knee injuries.
the proposed system can be used for robot-assisted knee rehabilitation in the early stages of recovery and can be easily adapted to the specific requirements of different patients.
the proposed device is a step forward towards the development of a fully adjustable robot-assisted rehabilitation exoskeleton.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel exoskeleton design that can be used for both active and passive exercises, and we provide a model based controller that can be utilized to achieve the desired interaction forces.
we developed a novel active device that enables robot-assisted rehabilitation of knee injuries with a perfect match between the human joint axes and device axes.

we have developed an innovative, adjustable, and compact robotic device capable of assisting the knee joint in the sagittal plane and that is capable of accommodating the transitional movements of the joint.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a self-adjusting exoskeleton can be designed to be compact, light-weight, and capable of providing a high level of assistance during the rehabilitation therapy.
the proposed system is able to support a wide range of patients, including children, with different knee joint axes, without the need of a time consuming calibration process.

by combining a self-adjusting mechanism and an active control of the joint axes, it is possible to achieve a perfect match between the axes of the human joint and the exoskeleton axes, thus guaranteeing ergonomics and comfort throughout the rehabilitation process.
